title: Ecclesiastes 1
paragraphs: ¹ These are the words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem. ² Meaningless, meaningless, says the Teacher — utterly meaningless. What do people gain from all their labor under the sun? ³ ⁴ One generation comes and another goes, but the earth endures forever. ⁵ The sun rises and the sun sets, hurrying back to where it rises.

⁶ The wind blows south, then swings to the north; round and round it goes, returning on its circuit. ⁷ All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full. The rivers run back to their source and flow again. ⁸ Everything is exhausting — more than words can say. The eye is never satisfied with seeing, nor the ear with hearing. ⁹ What has been will be again; what has been done will be done again. There is nothing new under the sun. ¹⁰ Is there anything of which you can say, "Look, this is new"? It has already existed in the ages before us.

¹¹ There is no memory of former things, and those who come after will not be remembered by those who follow. ¹² I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem. ¹³ I set my mind to search out and explore everything done under heaven by wisdom — a heavy burden God has given to humanity. ¹⁴ I have seen all the things done under the sun, and they are all meaningless, a chasing after the wind. ¹⁵ What is crooked cannot be straightened; what is missing cannot be counted.

¹⁶ I said to myself, "I have grown in wisdom beyond all who ruled Jerusalem before me; I have experienced great wisdom and knowledge." ¹⁷ So I set my mind to understand wisdom, and also madness and folly — but I came to see that this too is a chasing after the wind. ¹⁸ For with much wisdom comes much sorrow; the more knowledge, the more grief.
